Great Nigeria Insurance Plc (GNI) has said it is repositioning its business with new investors and management to improve service delivery and strengthen its capacity to pay claims. The company said the repositioning includes a faster claims process supported by technology and a strengthened capital base to accommodate larger risks.
The managing director and chief executive officer, Shola Osho, disclosed this at a professional brokers’ evening held in Abuja on Thursday. Osho said GNI would pay claims within 48 hours after a discharge voucher had been issued. She said the company’s operations would place emphasis on customer service and the settlement of claims.
The chairman of Board GNI, Tajudeen Idowu said with new investors, the company is ready to for business having recorded steady financial growth between 2023 and 2025, alongside a N15.6 billion capital injection through private placements.
He said: “Now we prioritise the payment of claims.Within the shortest period of time we came in as new investors,we have paid out N4 billion claims. We are ready and will ensure that we give our customers the peace and confidence to do business with us by prompt payments of claims when ever need arises.”
The chairman for Abuja Area Committee, Ojo Richards said the most important promise any insurance company can give to insurance consumers including brokers is claims settlements.” The company has promised that for every discharged claims,they are going to make payment within 48 hours.
This is goodnews and if it is being kept, definitely the insurance industry in Nigeria is going to improve on higher pedestal.”
Speaking earlier, the president of the Nigerian Council of Registered Insurance Brokers (NCRIB), Ekeoma Esther Ezeibe, FCIB urged insurance brokers to share industry challenges with the council to enable timely intervention.
Represented by the secretary, Tope Aderemola highlighted ongoing initiatives, including the insurance mediation project, training programmes and opportunities for members to improve their professional practice.
Another Broker and vice chairman of the Nigeria Council of Registered Insurance Brokers, Abuja Area Committee Amedu Emmanuel said GNI is is now repositioned.
Emmanuel called on citizens to take insurance very serious.”When everybody at the micro and macro level patronise insurance companies,it is going to add value to the economy and it will increase economic activities in the nation.”Emmanuel said.
The manager, Corporate Communications and Brand Management of GNI Benjamin Enem said the target of the event was to win back the confidence of brokers.
The event brought together stakeholders in the insurance industry and was an evening of talks towards moving the sector forward.
